summary: Mostly implementable: the secret store, CLI and Graph auth flows are well specified, but the biggest gap is plugin-config loading, where the ADR leaves open orphan or missing config files, the Dhall import policy, and how instances sharing a tokenKey are checked against each other.

questions.text: What does root preparation do with a plugin config file whose plugin is not installed (fail the root, ignore it, or block uninstall)?
questions.reason: Decides whether a fresh clone missing a plugin can be opened at all; the ADR only says malformed config fails the whole root and that installation creates no instances.

questions.text: May plugin config files use Dhall imports (relative, env, remote), or must they be hermetic?
questions.reason: Sets the decoder's import policy and what RootOpening/EvolutionStore must capture; the ADR requires snapshot files rather than ambient ones, but calls only secret files hermetic.

questions.text: Who validates that instances sharing a DeviceCode tokenKey declare the same tenant, clientId and scopes, given that validateConfig sees one instance?
questions.reason: A mismatch silently narrows the scopes of a shared refresh token; the ADR says compatible instances repeat the combined scopes and refresh must not narrow them, but its validator is per instance only.

questions.text: Are SecretNames case-sensitive, and how are case-only collisions handled on case-insensitive filesystems?
questions.reason: Two distinct names can map to one .dhall file and silently overwrite each other; the ADR defines the allowed characters and says the store must work on the supported targets, but says nothing about case or length.

questions.text: Where is the secret-store ignore rule installed, and what happens outside a Git work tree or when it cannot be written?
questions.reason: This is the guarantee that keeps secrets out of Git; the ADR requires installing an ignore rule before any write, but not where it goes or what to do on failure.

questions.text: Is a missing config file for an installed plugin treated as zero instances, or is the file required?
questions.reason: Changes RootStore loading and whether install or scaffold must create the file; the ADR names a well-known file per plugin and says installation creates no instances.

questions.text: What does secret list do with entries in .kyyn/secrets/ that are not <valid-name>.dhall files?
questions.reason: Decides whether list can fail and how cancellation leftovers are handled; the ADR says only that list returns sorted names and that corrupt storage is an operational failure.

questions.text: What are the config record shapes for Graph Mail, Meetings and Files, and do they all embed GraphAuth?
questions.reason: These persisted shapes drive the generated union, the validators and endpoint resolution; the ADR defines only CalendarConfig, and for the other types lists permissions, not fields.

questions.text: What are the syntax and uniqueness rules for instance names, and does a duplicate name fail root preparation?
questions.reason: Instance name keys identity and evidence history and is a CLI argument; the ADR gives bindings syntax and uniqueness rules but gives names none.

questions.text: Is validateConfig mandatory for every connector type, or optional with an empty report by default?
questions.reason: Changes the registration data shape and the scaffold output; the ADR says PrepareRoot retains the compiled validators and marks only login as optional.

questions.text: Are binding errors (invalid identifier, reserved word, collision) root-validation failures that block acceptance, or only generation-time errors?
questions.reason: Decides whether a colliding config can be accepted; the ADR sets the binding rules and says to report collisions, but not at which stage.

questions.text: Should the pure validator reject Graph auth-mode/endpoint combinations that Graph does not support, or should they fail only at invocation?
questions.reason: Decides whether such configs block acceptance; the ADR asks for explicit errors and for the sharedCalendar scope check in the validator, but not where the other checks go.
